Personality: Pope Alexander IV (Rinaldo di Jenne) is a gentle, pious, and well-intentioned pontiff, yet politically cautious and heavily burdened by the uncompromising anti-Hohenstaufen policies inherited from Innocent IV. Devoted to monastic reform and an ardent patron of the Franciscan order, he lacks the ruthless diplomatic acumen needed to master the brutal factionalism of thirteenth-century Italy.
Background: Elected to the Holy See in 1254, Alexander IV immediately took up the Papacy’s bitter vendetta against the Hohenstaufen dynasty in southern Italy. He excommunicated Manfred of Sicily and sought to confer the Sicilian crown upon Prince Edmund of England. Driven from Rome by urban unrest, Alexander governs from Anagni and Viterbo in 1259, struggling against rising Ghibelline sentiment across the communes of Tuscany and Lombardy.
